074/**
075 * This Interface presents a {@link RowSet} column presented by the visual
076 * components in the Seesaw library. It has default methods supporting binding
077 * a {@linkplain RowSet} column to this component, DBMS access with type conversion,
078 * undo/redo, validation, decoration. Most of these default methods bounce
079 * to an internal SsCommon class and would be declared final if java
080 * supported that. A database column is associated
081 * with this component via {@link RowsModel#bind(SsComponent,String) }.
082 * There are only two methods, and the Hook, that need to be implemented
083 * by the visual component: {@link #cleanField() }, {@link #getSsComponentHook() }.
084 * See {@link Hook} for a complete example.
085 * <p>
086 * The basic components for application use and/or subclassing are found in
087 * <a href="../core/package-summary.html">core components</a>.
088 * They are subclassed into a
089 * <a href="../package-summary.html">compatibility layer</a>
090 * as a replacement for the
091 * <a href="https://github.com/bpangburn/swingset">original SwingSet library</a>.
092 * <p>
093 * There are several methods that are typically overridden; they
094 * perform customization, receive notification, and do verification:
095 * {@link #customInit() },
096 * {@link #checkColumnType(JDBCType) }, {@link #metadataChange() },
097 * {@link #finishBind() }, {@link #baseValidate() }, {@link #componentValidate()},
098 * and {@link #createDefaultDecorator()}. Component developers should be aware
099 * of the method {@link #isComposite()}; override it to return true if the
100 * component contains JComponents and some of these descendant components may
101 * be focused.
102 * <p>
103 * The methods for reading and updating database columns are
104 * {@link #getColumnText() getColumn*()} and {@link #setColumnText(String) setColumn*}.
105 * With {@link #getColumnText() }, {@link #setColumnText(String) }
106 * and {@link #getColumnObject(Class) } values are converted as needed,
107 * see {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources.ConvertType}.
108 * For unhandled {@code JDBCType}s, {@link #getColumn() }
109 * and {@link #setColumn(Object) } are available;
110 * see {@link #setColumnReader(DbReader)}
111 * and {@link #setColumnUpdater(DbUpdater) }.
112 * <p>
113 * There are methods about column state, status and metadata;
114 * like {@link #getAllowNull() [sg]etAllowNull()}, {@link #isDirty() },
115 * {@link #getColumnJDBCType() }.
116 * <p>
117 * There are multiple levels of validation.
118 * The validators are executed in the
119 * following order, see {@link allValidate};
120 * if there's an error, validation stops, and see {@link ValidationResult}.
121 * <ol>
122 * <li>{@code baseValidate()} - method, defaults true<br>
123 * This checks that the SsComponent's value is more or less correct.
124 * For example a mask formatter's valid indicator,
125 * {@link javax.swing.JFormattedTextField#isEditValid};
126 * or a {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsTextField} subclass could check that there's only characters.
127 * <li>{@code componentValidate()} - method default true<br>
128 * A subclass of something that does baseValidate, can use this for more
129 * specific validation.
130 * <li>optionally check rowsModel.hasError(SsComponent)
131 * <li>{@code pluginValidate} - Application specific validation, per component instance.
132 * <br>
133 * Set at run time with {@link #setPluginValidator(Validator)}.
134 * For example check for specific values; or other columns or ...
135 * Can apply constraints while editing and avoid errors at commit.
136 * </ol>
137 * <p>
138 * There are {@link Decorator}s that visually indicate the components state.
139 * <p>
140 * When creating an SsComponent, typical usage: {@snippet lang="java":
141 *     class MyComponent extends SomeJComponent implements SsComponent {
142 *         MyComponent() {
143 *             // ...
144 *             // finishSsCommon() MUST BE CALLED AT END OF CONSTRUCTOR
145 *             finishSsCommon(); // @link substring="finishSsCommon" target="SsComponent#finishSsCommon"
146 *         }
147 *     }
148 * }
149 */
150public interface SsComponent extends RSC {
151  /**
152   * Initialize component to an empty or default value.
153   * Action could be conditioned on getAllowNull() or whatever.
154   */
155  void cleanField();
156
157  /**
158   * Return the {@linkplain Hook} used by SsCommon.
159   * An SsComponent must create a Hook.
160   * See {@link Hook} for a complete example.
161   * <p>
162   * <b>Generally should not be used except by SsCommon</b>.
163   * @return Hook
164   */
165  Hook getSsComponentHook();
166
167  /**
168   * An SsComponent must create a Hook. The hook is used by the Seesaw library
169   * to tell the component to read and display the current database value.
170   * Here's a complete example based on {@link SsCheckBox}.
171   * {@snippet lang="java" class=MyCheckBox region=hook_example}
172   * <p>
173   * <b>Generally should not be used except by SsCommon</b>.
174   */
175  abstract class Hook {
176    private final SsComponent ssComponent;
177
178    /**
179     * Create.
180     * @param ssComponent
181     */
182    protected Hook(SsComponent ssComponent) {
183      this.ssComponent = ssComponent;
184    }
185
186    /**
187     * Updates the value stored and displayed in the SwingSet component
188     * based on value obtained from the database with getColumn*().
189     * <p>
190     * Before this method, invoked by SsCommon, is called the component's
191     * listener is removed; it is restored when the call returns.
192     * The idea is to prevent event loops.
193     */
194    protected abstract void updateSsComponent();
195
196    /**
197     * Return the listener used by this SsComponent to detect changes
198     * in value for the current component.
199     * <p>
200     * A component generally has exactly one listener for
201     * detecting JComponent changes related to a database column, so this method
202     * will only be called one time in the SsCommon constructor to obtain
203     * that listener.
204     * <p>
205     * Usually the developer returns an instance of an inner class
206     * that implements the appropriate listener for the superclass
207     * JComponent, for example ItemListener for an SsComponent class
208     * extending JCheckBox, ChangeListener for a class extending JSlider.
209     * <p>
210     * If the component is JTextComponent then the implementation can return
211     * an instance of {@link SsTextSupport#getSsDocumentListener(JTextComponent) }
212     * which helps with per keystroke component decoration.
213     * For example: {@snippet :
214     *     protected SsDocumentListener getSsComponentListener() {
215     *         return SsTextSupport.getSsDocumentListener(TextField.this);
216     *     }
217     * }
218     * But typically, just subclass {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsTextField}
219     * and it's taken care of.
220     *
221     * @return event listener that triggers database column update
222     */
223    protected abstract EventListener getSsComponentListener();
224
225    /**
226     * Method to add SsComponent's listener.
227     *
228     * @param eventListener
229     */
230    protected abstract void addSsComponentListener(EventListener eventListener);
231
232    /**
233     * Method to remove SsComponent's listener.
234     *
235     * @param eventListener
236     */
237    protected abstract void removeSsComponentListener(EventListener eventListener);
238
239    private SsCommon ssCommon;
240    /**
241     * Returns ssCommon for the current Swingset component.
242     *
243     * @return common SwingSet component data and methods
244     */
245    final SsCommon getSsCommon() {
246      if (ssCommon == null)
247        ssCommon = SsCommon.createStart(ssComponent);
248      return ssCommon;
249    }
250
251    /**
252     * Invoked by ssComponent.finishSsCommon.
253     */
254    final void finishSsCommon() {
255      // Make sure ssCommon is initialized before doing createFinish.
256      // createFinish invokes the SsComponent to initialize some
257      // things; and SsComponent may use getSsCommon. Don't want to
258      // construct a 2nd SsCommon.
259      getSsCommon();
260      SsCommon ssCommon2 = SsCommon.createFinish(ssComponent, ssCommon);
261      if (ssCommon != ssCommon2) {
262        throw new IllegalStateException("Multiple SsCommon created");
263      }
264    }
265  }
266
267  ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
268  //
269  // The methods beyond this point have default implementations.
270  //
271  // The first group are commonly overriden.
272  //
273  // There are also some validation/decoration related methods near the end
274  // of this file that are commonly overridden:
275  //            baseValidate, componentValidate, createDefaultDecorator.
276  //
277
278  /**
279   * Method to allow Developer to add functionality when SwingSet component is
280   * instantiated.
281   * <p>
282   * It will actually be called from SsCommon.init() once the SsCommon data member
283   * is instantiated.
284   */
285  default void customInit() {}
286
287  /**
288   * Invoked during bind, component should verify that the database column's
289   * JDBCType is ok and handled by this component.
290   *
291   * @param jdbcType column JDBCType
292   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if can't handle JDBCType
293   */
294  default void checkColumnType(JDBCType jdbcType) throws IllegalArgumentException {}
295
296  /**
297   * This is overriden to return true by components that are made up of
298   * other components; and some of those contained components might get
299   * the focus. Examples are
300   * {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsImage} and DbDatePicker.
301   * @return
302   */
303  // isComposite component usually has
304  // comp != comp.getFocusTarget() || comp != comp.getDecorateTarget()
305  default boolean isComposite() {
306    return false;
307  }
308
309  /**
310   * Override this method for notification of a change in metadata.
311   * Typically from setRowSet() or bind().
312   */
313  default void metadataChange() {}
314
315  /**
316   * Invoked by the infrastructure at the end of bind;
317   * default sets up primary keys for CachedRowSet.
318   * Invoke super if override.
319   */
320  // TODO: currently called once per column, only needed once per RowSet?
321  default void finishBind() {
322    // Primary keys for SyncResolver, joins
323    if (getRowSet() instanceof CachedRowSet)
324      SsUtils.setupDefaultPrimaryKeys(this);
325  }

346  /**

370  /**
371   * Indicate whether or not the Component has been bound to a RowSet.

391  /**
392   * Setup additional focus transfer keys.

405  /**

410   * @return the database value as String to display in the SsComponent, may be from undo/redo stack.
411   */

417  /**

419   * as returned by {@link RowSet#getObject(int) }.

423   */
424  // TODO: put this in RSC?
425  default Object getColumnObject() {
426    return getSsCommon().getColumnObject();
427  }

429  /** {@inheritDoc } */
430  @Override
431  default<T> T getColumnObject(Class<T> clazz) {
432    return getSsCommon().getColumnObject(clazz);
433  }

435  /**
436   * Returns the Array for the bound database column
437   * as returned by {@link RowSet#getArray(int) }.
438   * <p>
439   * @return the value to display in the SsComponent, may be from undo/redo stack.

443  }

445  /**
446   * Return the value of the bound database column using the SsComponent's
447   * {@link DbReader}. See {@link #getColumnReader() }.
448   * NPE if no columnReader. Useful for dealing with JDBCTypes not handled
449   * internally.
450   *
451   * @return the value to display in the SsComponent, may be from undo/redo stack.
452   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
453   */
454  default Object getColumn() throws SQLException {
455    return getSsCommon().getColumn();
456  }
457
458  /**
459   * Get the columnReader used by {@link #getColumn()} and internally,
460   * when not null, for capturing initial value for undo/redo.
461   * This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not
462   * handled internally, like BLOB and VARBINARY.
463   * For exampe, see {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsImage} source code.
464   *
465   * The {@code columnReader} is typically invoked like
466   * {@code .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp)}.
467   * The comp is rarely used, and provided for complex situations. The
468   * columnReader return the value fetched from the datbase.
469   *
470   * @return the DbReader used to fetch values from the database
471   */
472  default DbReader<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent> getColumnReader() {
473    return getSsCommon().getColumnReader();
474  }
475
476  /**
477   * Set the columnReader used by {@link #getColumn()} and internally for capturing
478   * initial value. This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not
479   * handled internally, like BLOB and VARBINARY.
480   * For exampe, see {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsImage} source code.
481   *
482   * The {@code columnReader} is typically invoked like
483   * {@code .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp)}.
484   * The comp is rarely used, and provided just in case.
485   * For example with a BLOB or BINARY column
486   * {@snippet lang="java" class=DbReaderDbUpdater region=setColumnReader}
487   * @param columnReader the DbReader used to fetch values from the database
488   */
489  default void setColumnReader(DbReader<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent> columnReader) {
490    getSsCommon().setColumnReader(columnReader);
491  }
492
493  /**
494   * Used when making a change to the database.
495   * Typically used by a component listener. It avoids extra RowSet events.
496   * See {@link Hook} for example usage.
497   * May bring up a dialog if there is no row to change, which would
498   * usually indicate some kind of internal error.
499   * @param r code that changes the database
500   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
501   */
502  default void dbChange(RunnableSQL r) throws SQLException {
503    getSsCommon().dbChange(r);
504  }
505
506  /**
507   * Updates the value of the bound database column;
508   * method used by SwingSet component listeners to update the underlying RowSet.
509   * The real action, like null handling and conversion checking, happens
510   * in {@link RowSetOps#updateColumnText(dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.SsComponent, java.lang.String) }.
511   * Does not commit the update row.
512   *
513   * @param columnText the value to set in the bound database column
514   * @return true if no error
515   */
516  default boolean setColumnText(String columnText) {
517    return getSsCommon().setColumnText(columnText);
518  }
519
520  /**
521   * Updates the value of the bound database column;
522   * method used by SwingSet component listeners to update the underlying RowSet.
523   * Does not commit the update row.
524   *
525   * @param columnObject the value to set in the bound database column
526   * @return true if no error
527   */
528  default boolean setColumnObject(Object columnObject) {
529    return getSsCommon().setColumnObject(columnObject);
530  }
531
532  /**
533   * Updates the bound database column with the specified Array.
534   * <p>
535   * Used for List or other component where multiple items can be selected.
536   * See {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsList1} and
537   * {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.models.DbCollection} for low level
538   * details on how arrays are read and written.
539   * Does not commit the update row.
540   *
541   * @param columnArray Array to write to bound database column
542   * @return true if no error
543   * @throws SQLException thrown if there is a problem writing the array to the
544   *                      RowSet
545   */
546  default boolean setColumnArray(Array columnArray) throws SQLException {
547    return getSsCommon().setColumnArray(columnArray);
548  }
549
550  /**
551   * Updates the value of the bound database column;
552   * method used by SwingSet component listeners to update the underlying RowSet.
553   * Sets the value of the bound database column using the SsComponent's
554   * {@link DbUpdater}. See {@link #getColumnUpdater() }.
555   * NPE if no columnUpdater. Useful for dealing with JDBCTypes not handled
556   * internally.
557   * Does not commit the update row.
558   *
559   * @param value to write to the database, may write to the undo/redo stack.
560   * @return true if no error
561   */
562  default boolean setColumn(Object value) {
563    return getSsCommon().setColumn(value);
564  }
565
566  /**
567   * Get the columnUpdater used by {@link #setColumn(Object)}.
568   * This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not

570   * For exampe, see {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsImage} source code.
571   *
572   * The {@code columnUpdater} is typically invoked like
573   * {@code .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp, value)}.
574   * The comp is rarely used, and provided for complex situations.
575   *
576   * @return the DbUpdater used to update to the database
577   */
578  default DbUpdater<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent, Object> getColumnUpdater() {
579    return getSsCommon().getColumnUpdater();
580  }
581
582  /**
583   * Set the columnUpdater used by {@link #setColumn(Object)}.
584   * This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not

586   * For exampe, see {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.SsImage} source code.
587   *
588   * The {@code columnUpdater} is typically invoked like
589   * {@code .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp, value)}.
590   * The comp is rarely used, and provided just in case.
591   * For example with a BLOB or BINARY column:
592   * {@snippet lang="java" class=DbReaderDbUpdater region=setColumnUpdater}
593   *
594   * @param columnUpdater the DbUpdater used to update the database
595   */
596  default void setColumnUpdater(DbUpdater<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent, Object> columnUpdater) {
597    getSsCommon().setColumnUpdater(columnUpdater);
598  }

653  /**
654   * Returns the index of the database column to which the SwingSet component is

871  /**
872   * Install the specified pluginValidator into this component.
873   * Each instance can have a unique validator.
874   * This is run after all the other validations succeed.
875   * @param pluginValidator validator to install
876   */
877  default void setPluginValidator(Validator pluginValidator) {
878    getSsCommon().setPluginValidator(pluginValidator);
879  }

881  /**
882   * Override this to do a low level validation of whether or not the
883   * component data is valid.
884   * For example, a mask formatter indicates valid; generally simple
885   * constraints that are context independent; e.g. {@literal month <= 12}.
886   * There may be additional checks defined by {@link #componentValidate() }
887   * and/or a {@link Validator}, see
888   * {@link #setPluginValidator(Validator) }; those are checked after baseValidate.
889   * The default implementation returns true.
890   *
891   * @return false for error in data, otherwise true
892   */
893  //{@link #setPluginValidator(dev.visdb.seesaw.decorators.Validator) }; those are check after baseValidate.
894  default boolean baseValidate() {
895    return true;
896  }
897
898  /**
899   * This has component specific validation, it is called after baseValidate.
900   * @return true if successful validation for the type of component
901   */
902  default boolean componentValidate() {
903    return true;
904  }
905
906  /**
907   * The results of doing SsComponent validations.
908   *
909   * @param base result of baseValidate()
910   * @param comp result of base and componentValidate()
911   * @param other this component is the target of an error event,
912   * see {@link RowsModel#hasError(SsComponent) }
913   * @param plugin result of pluginValidate
914   * @param all true if everything validated
915   */
916  record ValidationResult(boolean base, boolean comp, boolean other, boolean plugin, boolean all) {}
917
918  /**
919   * Run the validators: baseValidate, componentValidate,
920   * possibly check RowsModel.hasError(),
921   * pluginValidate.
922   * The checks are done in order, they stop with any failure.
923   * @return result
924   */
925  default ValidationResult allValidate() {
926    boolean baseValid = baseValidate();
927    boolean compValid = baseValid && componentValidate();
928    boolean otherValid = compValid;
929    if (compValid && !getSsCommon().skipValidateHasError) {
930      RowsModel rowsModel = getRowsModel();
931      if (rowsModel != null && rowsModel.getRowSet() != null)
932        otherValid = !rowsModel.hasError(this);
933    }
934    boolean pluginValid = otherValid && getSsCommon().pluginValidate();
935
936    return new ValidationResult(baseValid, compValid, otherValid, pluginValid, pluginValid);
937  }
